name: Fibre terminal
simple: In a building of your internet company, a big box listens to the light from many streets and tells each house when it may send.
technical: The OLT (optical line terminal) at the exchange: it runs the PON (grants each home its upstream slots, encrypts what goes down), then bridges each home’s Ethernet frames on with Q-in-Q tags towards the BNG.

up.simple: The fibre terminal takes your parcel out of its light envelope and puts two stickers on it: one for your street, one for your home.
up.technical: The OLT ends XGS-PON (the XGEM header comes off), bridges the Ethernet frame on and pushes two 802.1ad tags: S-VLAN 101 for the PON, C-VLAN 2042 for this home.

down.simple: The fibre terminal peels off the two stickers, puts your parcel in a light envelope with your house number and sends it down the glass thread to every house on your street.
down.technical: The OLT pops the Q-in-Q tags, maps the frame to XGEM Port-ID 1127, encrypts it with that port’s AES key and broadcasts it down the PON.
